name: Cinnamon Coffee Protein Shake

ingredients.name: clean unsweetened protein powder (Previnex or similar)
natural almond butter (no added sugar or oils)

steps: Add the protein powder, cooled coffee, almond butter, cinnamon, and water or ice to a blender or shaker.
Blend or shake until smooth. Drink right away.
leftovers: Best made fresh. You can portion the powder, cinnamon, and a little almond butter the night before.

name: Green Protein Shake

ingredients.name: clean unsweetened protein powder (Previnex or similar)
natural peanut butter (unsalted, no added sugar)

steps: Pack the spinach into a blender with the water, protein powder, peanut butter, cinnamon, and ice.
Blend until the spinach disappears and the shake is smooth.
leftovers: Blend fresh. Spinach and powder can be pre-portioned.

name: Turkey & Spinach Breakfast Skillet
steps: Warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 2 minutes until it softens.
Add the turkey, garlic, smoked paprika, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains, about 6–8 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and wilt 1 minute. Taste and add a little pepper or paprika rather than more salt if you want more flavor.
leftovers: Keeps 2 days in the fridge. Reheat gently in a skillet with a splash of water.

name: Salmon Breakfast Plate
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Place the salmon on a small pan, season with a pinch of salt, pepper, and lemon juice, and bake 10–12 minutes until it flakes. Skip this step if you already have leftover baked salmon.
Slice the avocado and cucumber. Plate with the salmon, a little more lemon, and dill.
leftovers: This is one of the best uses for leftover baked salmon. Eat the avocado fresh.

name: Chicken & Zucchini Morning Hash
steps: Warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken with a pinch of salt, pepper, and oregano until cooked through, about 6 minutes. Set aside if the pan is crowded.
Add the onion, pepper, and zucchini. Sauté 5–6 minutes until tender-crisp. Return the chicken, toss, and serve.
leftovers: Keeps 2–3 days. Reheat in a skillet so the zucchini does not go soggy in the microwave.

name: Mushroom-Kale Sauté with Turkey
steps: Warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the turkey with a pinch of salt, pepper, and thyme until cooked through, about 5–6 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and garlic. Cook 3 minutes until the mushrooms give off liquid.
Add the kale and toss until wilted, 1–2 minutes. Finish with lemon juice.
leftovers: Good the next day. The kale softens more on reheating, which is fine.

name: Garlic Shrimp, Avocado & Greens
steps: Pat the shrimp dry. Warm the olive oil over medium heat and cook the garlic 20 seconds.
Add the shrimp, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Cook 1–2 minutes per side until just pink and opaque. Do not overcook.
Pile the greens and sliced avocado on a plate. Top with the shrimp, lemon juice, and parsley.
leftovers: Cook the shrimp ahead and chill. Assemble with avocado just before eating. Shrimp is naturally higher in sodium; skip extra salt.

name: Cauliflower Hash with Turkey
steps: Warm the olive oil in a large skillet. Cook the turkey with cumin, paprika, a pinch of salt, and pepper until browned, about 6 minutes.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and cauliflower rice. Cook 5–6 minutes, stirring, until the cauliflower is tender and any liquid cooks off.
leftovers: Excellent meal-prep breakfast. Makes a good double batch. Reheats well in a skillet.

name: Pork Medallions with Asparagus
steps: Season the pork with rosemary, a pinch of salt, and pepper.
Warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the medallions 2–3 minutes per side until just cooked through (145°F). Transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, sauté the asparagus and garlic 3–4 minutes until tender-crisp. Add lemon juice and serve with the pork.
leftovers: A great use for leftover roasted pork tenderloin. Just warm the slices and sauté fresh asparagus.

name: Broccoli & Chicken Morning Sauté
steps: Warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken with a pinch of salt and pepper until cooked through, about 5–6 minutes. Set aside.
Add the broccoli and 2 tablespoons water. Cover 2–3 minutes to steam, then uncover, add garlic and crushed red pepper, and sauté 2 minutes.
Return the chicken, toss with lemon juice, and serve.
leftovers: Works with leftover chicken. Reheat quickly so the broccoli stays bright.

name: Smoky Turkey Patties with Peppers
steps: Mix the turkey with smoked paprika, onion powder, mustard powder, salt, and pepper. Form 4 thin patties.
Warm 1 teaspoon olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the patties 4–5 minutes per side until cooked through. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining teaspoon of oil, then the peppers and onion. Sauté 5–6 minutes until soft and slightly browned. Serve 2 patties with half the peppers per plate.
leftovers: Patties keep 3 days and freeze well. Reheat in a skillet or oven. This recipe makes 2 breakfasts.

name: Trout & Wilted Spinach
steps: Season the trout with a pinch of salt, pepper, and dill.
Warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the trout skin-side down (if it has skin) 3–4 minutes, flip, and cook 2–3 minutes more until it flakes.
Push the fish to the side or plate it. Add garlic and spinach to the pan and wilt 1 minute. Finish with lemon and serve beside the trout.
leftovers: Best fresh, but leftover trout is also good cold with the spinach rewarmed.

name: Avocado Stuffed with Seasoned Turkey
steps: Cook the turkey in a small skillet with the olive oil, garlic powder, paprika, a pinch of salt, and pepper until cooked through, about 6–8 minutes.
Halve an avocado and leave the shell on one half (save the rest for later). Loosen the flesh a little with a spoon.
Pile the turkey into the avocado half. Add lemon juice and serve with cucumber slices.
leftovers: Cook a batch of seasoned turkey and keep it 2–3 days. Assemble with a fresh avocado half. The no-cook tag applies when the turkey is already cooked.

name: Walnut-Cinnamon Protein Bowl

ingredients.name: clean unsweetened protein powder (Previnex or similar)

steps: Stir the protein powder with just enough water to make a thick pudding. Add vanilla and most of the cinnamon.
Top with chopped walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. Drink coffee on the side if you like.
This is mild and spiced, not sweet — think breakfast pudding, not dessert.
leftovers: Mix fresh. Walnuts can be pre-chopped; stick to about 2 tablespoons (a half ounce).

name: Herb Cod over Sautéed Greens
steps: If the cod is not already cooked, season it with a pinch of salt and pepper and bake or pan-cook in 1/2 teaspoon olive oil until it flakes, about 8 minutes.
Sauté garlic in the remaining oil 20 seconds, add the greens, and wilt. Flake the cod over the top. Finish with lemon and parsley.
leftovers: Built for leftover baked white fish. A very light, high-protein start to the day.

name: Lemon Herb Chicken & Broccoli
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the chicken with 1 teaspoon olive oil, oregano, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Toss the broccoli with the remaining oil and garlic.
Spread on a sheet pan and roast 16–18 minutes, until the chicken is 165°F and the broccoli is browned at the edges.
Slice the chicken, squeeze lemon over everything, and divide into 2 servings.
leftovers: Perfect for 2 lunches. Keeps 3 days. Eat cold or reheat.

name: Salmon Salad over Greens
steps: Bake the salmon at 400°F for 10–12 minutes, seasoned with a pinch of salt, pepper, and a little lemon. Or use leftover salmon.
Toss the greens and cucumber with olive oil, remaining lemon, and dill. Flake the salmon over the top.
leftovers: Bake two fillets at once. Dress the greens just before eating so they stay crisp.

name: Turkey & Avocado Cabbage Wraps

ingredients.name: turkey breast (fresh roasted, not deli meat)

steps: If the turkey is raw, roast or skillet-cook it until 165°F, then slice. Soften the cabbage leaves by dipping them in hot water 20–30 seconds if they crack when folded.
Mash the avocado with lemon, pepper, and a pinch of salt. Spread on the leaves, add turkey and cucumber, and wrap.
leftovers: Use leftover roasted turkey — never packaged deli meat, which is processed and salty. The no-cook tag applies when the turkey is already cooked.

name: Shrimp & Zucchini Sauté
steps: Warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the zucchini 3–4 minutes until just tender. Push to the side.
Add the shrimp, garlic, a pinch of salt, pepper, and crushed red pepper. Cook 1–2 minutes per side until opaque.
Toss together, finish with lemon and parsley. Skip extra salt — shrimp already brings sodium.
leftovers: Best fresh. Leftover shrimp is fine cold the next day over greens.

name: Cod with Roasted Brussels Sprouts
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the Brussels sprouts with the olive oil, garlic, thyme, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Roast 12 minutes.
Push the sprouts aside, add the cod, and roast 8–10 minutes more until the fish flakes and the sprouts are browned.
Squeeze lemon over the pan and serve.
leftovers: The sprouts reheat well. The fish is best the same day or gently warmed the next.

name: Chicken, Pepper & Onion Sheet Pan

ingredients.name: skinless chicken breast, cut into strips

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss everything on a sheet pan with the oil and spices.
Roast 20–22 minutes, stirring once, until the chicken is cooked through and the peppers are soft and browned in spots.
Divide into 2 lunches.
leftovers: A workhorse meal-prep lunch. Keeps 3 days. Good cold or reheated.

name: Bison Cabbage Cups
steps: Warm the olive oil in a skillet. Cook the onion and pepper 3 minutes. Add the bison, garlic, cumin, paprika, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Cook until browned and done, about 6 minutes.
Spoon into cabbage leaves and eat like small wraps.
This is an occasional, modest-portion lunch — 4 ounces of bison, not a large burger.
leftovers: The filling keeps 2 days. Because bison is a red meat, keep it to 1–2 times a week.

name: Rainbow Trout with Asparagus
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Place the trout and asparagus on a sheet pan. Drizzle with olive oil, and season with garlic, dill, a pinch of salt, and pepper.
Roast 12–15 minutes until the fish flakes and the asparagus is tender-crisp. Finish with lemon.
leftovers: Good cold the next day. Fatty fish like trout is worth eating a few times a week.

name: Chicken Cauliflower Bowl
steps: Warm 1 teaspoon oil in a large skillet. Cook the chicken with a pinch of salt and pepper until done, about 6–7 minutes. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil, cauliflower, garlic, turmeric, and cumin. Cook 5–6 minutes until tender. Stir in the spinach to wilt, return the chicken, and finish with lemon.
Divide into 2 bowls.
leftovers: Holds 3 days. The turmeric and lemon keep it from tasting flat without extra salt.

name: Grilled Shrimp Salad with Walnuts
steps: Toss the shrimp with half the oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Grill or skillet-cook 1–2 minutes per side until just opaque.
Toss the greens and cucumber with the remaining oil and lemon. Top with shrimp and a small sprinkle of walnuts (about 2 teaspoons — a modest portion).
leftovers: Cook extra shrimp for tomorrow. Add walnuts and dressing just before eating.

name: Pork Tenderloin & Green Beans
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Season the pork with thyme, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Roast 16–18 minutes until 145°F, or skillet-sear and finish in the oven.
Meanwhile, sauté or steam the green beans with garlic and 1 teaspoon oil until tender-crisp. Toss with lemon and the almonds (a small sprinkle, not a handful).
Rest the pork 5 minutes, slice, and divide with the beans into 2 servings.
leftovers: Roast a whole tenderloin on Sunday and you have lunches ready. Slice only what you need.

name: Turkey & Mushroom Lettuce Cups
steps: Warm the olive oil in a skillet. Cook the onion, mushrooms, and turkey with garlic, thyme, a pinch of salt, and pepper until the turkey is done and the mushrooms have browned, about 8–10 minutes.
Spoon into lettuce leaves and eat right away.
leftovers: The filling keeps 3 days. Pack leaves separately so they stay crisp.

name: White Fish with Vinegar-Herb Cabbage Slaw
steps: Toss the cabbage with 2 teaspoons olive oil, the vinegar, dill, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Let it sit while you cook the fish — it softens slightly.
Season the fish and cook in the remaining teaspoon of oil over medium heat, 4–5 minutes per side, until it flakes. Or bake at 400°F for about 12 minutes.
Serve the fish on the slaw with a squeeze of lemon.
leftovers: The slaw actually improves after an hour. Fish is best the day it is cooked, or cold the next day.

name: Leftover Chicken & Broccoli Bowl
steps: Steam or skillet-sauté the broccoli with a splash of water until tender-crisp, about 4 minutes. Add the oil and garlic for the last minute.
Add the leftover chicken just to warm it. Finish with lemon, crushed red pepper, and black pepper. No extra salt needed if the chicken was already seasoned.
leftovers: This is the leftover recipe. Keep cooked chicken on hand for a 10-minute lunch.

name: Kale Salad with Salmon & Avocado
steps: Bake or skillet-cook the salmon until it flakes, about 10–12 minutes.
Massage the kale with olive oil, lemon, garlic, and a pinch of salt for 1 minute until it darkens and softens.
Top with flaked salmon and a quarter of an avocado, sliced. A quarter is plenty here because the salmon already brings healthy fat.
leftovers: Massaged kale holds up better than lettuce, so you can dress it ahead. Add avocado at the last minute.

name: Sheet-Pan Turkey, Peppers & Onions
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the turkey, peppers, and onion with oil and spices on a sheet pan.
Roast 18–20 minutes, stirring once, until the turkey is 165°F and the vegetables are browned at the edges.
Divide into 2 servings.
leftovers: A reliable two-lunch batch. Keeps 3 days.

name: Lemon Haddock & Steamed Broccoli
steps: Steam the broccoli until tender-crisp, about 5–6 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the haddock in the olive oil over medium heat, 4–5 minutes per side, or bake at 400°F for about 12 minutes, with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Plate together with lemon juice and parsley. Simple and clean.
leftovers: Best the day you cook it. A very low-sat-fat lunch when you want something light.

name: Sheet-Pan Salmon, Broccoli & Red Onion
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the broccoli and onion with 1 teaspoon oil, garlic, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread on a sheet pan and roast 8 minutes.
Add the salmon, brushed with the remaining oil, dill, and a little pepper. Roast 10 minutes more until the salmon flakes.
Finish with lemon and divide into 2 plates.
leftovers: Excellent next-day lunch, cold or gently reheated. Fatty fish is a weekly staple here.

name: Garlic Herb Chicken Thighs with Brussels Sprouts
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the thighs and Brussels sprouts with oil, garlic, rosemary, thyme, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread on a sheet pan, chicken in the center.
Roast 25–28 minutes until the chicken is 165°F and the sprouts are browned and crisp at the edges.
Finish with lemon. This is a little over 25 minutes, but it is almost all hands-off oven time.
leftovers: Skinless thighs stay juicier than breast as leftovers. Keeps 3 days.

name: Lemon Dill Trout with Asparagus
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Arrange the trout and asparagus on a sheet pan. Drizzle with oil and season with garlic, dill, a pinch of salt, and pepper.
Roast 12–15 minutes until the fish flakes. Squeeze lemon over both and serve.
leftovers: Lovely cold the next day. Trout is a fatty fish — good for a couple of dinners a week.

name: Shrimp & Cauliflower Rice Sauté
steps: Warm 1 teaspoon oil in a large skillet. Cook the onion 2 minutes, then add the cauliflower rice, garlic, and paprika. Cook 5–6 minutes until tender. Transfer to a bowl.
Add the remaining oil and the shrimp. Cook 1–2 minutes per side until just opaque. Skip extra salt if you can — shrimp is naturally salty.
Return the cauliflower, toss with lime and parsley, and divide into 2 bowls.
leftovers: The cauliflower rice keeps well; add freshly cooked shrimp if you can. Fine reheated once.

name: Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Cabbage Wedges
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Brush the cabbage wedges with 1 teaspoon oil, garlic, caraway or thyme, and a pinch of salt. Roast 10 minutes.
Season the pork and nestle it on the pan. Roast 15–18 minutes more, until the pork is 145°F and the cabbage is browned on the edges.
Rest the pork 5 minutes, slice, and serve with the wedges and a little lemon.
leftovers: Sliced pork and cabbage reheat well. A good Sunday roast for two dinners or a dinner plus lunch.

name: Lean Beef, Mushrooms & Spinach Skillet

ingredients.name: lean beef sirloin or loin, thinly sliced

steps: Warm 1 teaspoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the beef quickly, 1–2 minutes per side, until just browned. Do not overcook. Transfer to a plate. This is a modest 4 ounces of lean beef per person.
Add the remaining oil, onion, and mushrooms. Cook 5–6 minutes until browned. Add garlic and thyme for 30 seconds.
Add the spinach to wilt, return the beef and any juices, and toss with pepper. Taste before adding any more salt.
leftovers: Eat within 2 days. Keep lean beef and bison to 1–2 meals a week, in modest portions.

name: Bison & Pepper Skillet
steps: Warm the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and peppers 4 minutes.
Add the bison, garlic, and spices. Cook, breaking it up, until browned and done, about 6–7 minutes. This is 4 ounces of bison per person — a modest, occasional dinner.
Taste and add pepper or cumin before reaching for more salt.
leftovers: Makes a good lunch the next day in cabbage leaves. Limit red meat to 1–2 times a week.

name: Herb-Roasted Cod with Zucchini
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the zucchini with 1 teaspoon oil, garlic, oregano, and a pinch of salt. Roast 8 minutes.
Add the cod, brushed with the remaining oil and pepper. Roast 8–10 minutes until the fish flakes.
Finish with lemon and divide into 2 plates.
leftovers: A very low-sat-fat dinner. The fish is best the day you cook it.

name: Chicken & Mushroom Skillet
steps: Warm 1 teaspoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken with a pinch of salt, pepper, and some of the thyme until cooked through, about 6–7 minutes. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil and the mushrooms. Let them sit and brown, 5–6 minutes, then add garlic and the rest of the thyme.
Return the chicken, toss with lemon and parsley, and serve.
leftovers: Very leftover-friendly. The mushrooms soak up the lemon and thyme overnight.

name: Turkey-Stuffed Bell Peppers
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Place the pepper halves cut-side up in a baking dish.
Cook the onion, turkey, cauliflower, garlic, and spices in the olive oil until the turkey is done, about 8 minutes. Spoon into the peppers.
Bake 20 minutes until the peppers are tender. A little over 30 minutes total, but the steps stay simple.
leftovers: One of the best meal-prep dinners. Keeps 3 days and reheats in the oven or microwave.

name: Broiled Salmon with Garlic Kale
steps: Heat the broiler. Brush the salmon with 1 teaspoon oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Broil 8–10 minutes until it flakes (or bake at 400°F for 12 minutes).
Meanwhile, sauté the garlic in the remaining oil 20 seconds, add the kale and a splash of water, and cook until wilted but still green, 3–4 minutes.
Finish the kale with lemon and serve under the salmon.
leftovers: Salmon and kale both keep 1–2 days. A strong weekly staple for LDL-friendly omega-3s.

name: Sheet-Pan Chicken, Cauliflower & Broccoli
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the chicken and vegetables with oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer.
Roast 22–25 minutes, until the chicken is 165°F and the vegetables are browned.
Squeeze lemon over the pan and divide into 2 servings.
leftovers: A classic two-night sheet pan. Keeps 3 days and packs well.

name: Garlic Shrimp over Sautéed Spinach
steps: Warm 1 teaspoon oil in a large skillet. Cook half the garlic 20 seconds, add the spinach in handfuls, and wilt. Divide onto 2 plates.
Add the remaining oil, garlic, shrimp, crushed red pepper, and black pepper. Cook 1–2 minutes per side until just opaque. No extra salt.
Spoon the shrimp over the spinach and finish with lemon. Dinner in 15 minutes.
leftovers: Best fresh. Leftover shrimp is fine cold the next day. Spinach wilts more on reheat.

name: Trout with Green Beans & Almonds
steps: Bake or skillet-cook the trout with 1 teaspoon oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper until it flakes, about 10–12 minutes.

Meanwhile, sauté the green beans and garlic in the remaining oil until tender-crisp, 6–8 minutes. Toast the almonds in a dry corner of the pan for the last minute — 1 tablespoon per person is a modest portion.
Plate the trout with the beans, almonds, and lemon. This is a sauté, not a fry — keep the oil to the measured teaspoons.
leftovers: Green beans and trout keep 1–2 days. Add the almonds just before serving so they stay crisp.

name: Pork Medallions with Mushrooms & Onions
steps: Season the medallions with rosemary, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Warm 1 teaspoon oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the pork 2–3 minutes per side until 145°F. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil, mushrooms, and onion. Cook 6–8 minutes until browned and soft. Add garlic for the last 30 seconds.
Return the pork and any juices to the pan, toss, and serve.
leftovers: Reheats gently. Don't push leftover pork past a couple of days.

name: White Fish in Parchment with Vegetables
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Cut two large sheets of parchment (foil works if you don't have parchment).
Divide the vegetables between the sheets, top with the fish, oil, thyme, lemon slices, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Fold and crimp into sealed packets.
Bake 16–18 minutes. Open carefully — the steam is hot — and finish with parsley. The fish steams in its own juices, so it stays moist with very little oil.
leftovers: Best the night you make it. Packets can be assembled a few hours ahead and kept in the fridge until dinner.

name: Chicken Thighs with Cabbage
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F, or use a large oven-safe skillet. Season the thighs with paprika, a pinch of salt, and pepper.

Brown the chicken in 1 teaspoon oil, 3 minutes per side. Add the remaining oil, cabbage, onion, garlic, and caraway. Toss, then roast or bake 20–22 minutes until the chicken is 165°F and the cabbage is tender and browned.
Hands-off after the first sear. Total time is about 30 minutes.
leftovers: Cabbage and thighs reheat beautifully. A solid leftover dinner or lunch.

name: Baked Haddock with Peppers & Onions
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the peppers and onion with 1 teaspoon oil, half the paprika, and a pinch of salt. Roast 10 minutes.
Add the haddock, brushed with the remaining oil, paprika, and pepper. Bake 10 minutes more until the fish flakes.
Finish with lemon and parsley.
leftovers: Peppers and onions keep well; the fish is better the day you bake it.

name: Seasoned Turkey Patties with Roasted Broccoli
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Mix the turkey with the garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, oregano, salt, and pepper. Form 4 patties — no breadcrumbs needed if you handle them gently.
Toss the broccoli with 1 teaspoon oil and spread on a sheet pan with the patties, brushed with the remaining oil.
Roast 16–18 minutes, flipping the patties once, until the turkey is 165°F. Finish the broccoli with lemon.
leftovers: Patties freeze well and make an easy lunch. No filler or processed meat — just seasoned turkey.

name: Salmon with Roasted Garlic Brussels Sprouts
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the Brussels sprouts with 1 teaspoon oil, garlic, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Roast 10 minutes.
Add the salmon, brushed with the remaining oil and pepper. Roast 10 minutes more until the salmon flakes and the sprouts are crisp-edged.
Finish with lemon.
leftovers: A repeat-worthy weekly staple. Brussels sprouts reheat especially well.

name: Lean Beef & Broccoli Sauté

ingredients.name: lean beef sirloin or loin, thinly sliced

steps: Warm 1 teaspoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the beef quickly in a single layer, 1–2 minutes, until just browned. Set aside. This is 4 ounces of lean beef per person.
Add the remaining oil, broccoli, and a splash of water. Cover 3 minutes to steam, then uncover and add garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Return the beef, toss with green onions and pepper, and serve. No bottled sauce — the garlic, ginger, and pepper do the work. This is a sauté, not a fry.
leftovers: Eat within 2 days. Keep this to 1–2 modest red-meat meals a week.

name: Herb Chicken with Asparagus & Mushrooms
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Season the chicken with rosemary, a pinch of salt, and pepper, and place on a sheet pan with the mushrooms and asparagus. Drizzle with oil and scatter the garlic.
Roast 16–18 minutes until the chicken is 165°F. Finish with lemon and slice the chicken to serve.
leftovers: Slices nicely for lunch the next day.

name: Sheet-Pan Shrimp, Zucchini & Peppers
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the zucchini and peppers with 1 teaspoon oil, half the garlic, and some paprika. Roast 6 minutes.
Toss the shrimp with the remaining oil, garlic, paprika, and pepper. Add to the pan and roast 6 minutes more until just opaque.
Finish with lime. No extra salt — shrimp already has sodium.
leftovers: Good cold over greens the next day. Don't reheat shrimp too long or it turns rubbery.

name: Walnut-Herb Chicken with Green Beans
steps: Mash or finely chop the walnuts with the herbs, garlic, 1 teaspoon oil, lemon, and a pinch of salt to make a rough, cheese-free herb paste. This is a modest walnut portion — about 1 tablespoon per person.
Cook the chicken in the remaining oil over medium heat until 165°F, about 6 minutes per side, or bake at 400°F for 18 minutes. Steam or sauté the green beans until tender-crisp.
Spread the herb paste over the sliced chicken and serve with the beans.
leftovers: The herb paste keeps 2 days. Spread it on leftover chicken just before eating so it stays bright.

name: Scallops with Garlic Spinach & Cauliflower
steps: Steam or roast the cauliflower until tender, about 8–10 minutes.

Pat the scallops very dry. Warm 1 teaspoon oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the scallops 2 minutes per side until just opaque and browned. Do not crowd the pan. Set aside. Wet-packed scallops can be brined — skip extra salt either way.
Add the remaining oil, garlic, and spinach; wilt quickly. Plate the cauliflower and spinach, top with scallops, lemon, parsley, and pepper.
leftovers: Scallops are best the night you cook them. Use dry-packed if you can; they usually have less added sodium.

name: Chicken Thighs, Peppers & Onions

ingredients.name: skinless chicken thighs, cut into chunks

steps: Warm the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the thighs with smoked paprika, oregano, a pinch of salt, and pepper, about 5 minutes.
Add the peppers, onion, and garlic. Cook, stirring now and then, 12–15 minutes until the chicken is 165°F and the vegetables are soft and browned in spots.
A simple skillet dinner with a lot of flavor and no sauce to measure.
leftovers: Even better the next day. Keeps 3 days and makes an easy lunch.

name: Almonds & Cucumber
steps: Portion 1 ounce of almonds (about 23 almonds, or a small handful). Don't eat from the bag.
Slice the cucumber, add a little lemon if you like, and eat alongside the almonds.
leftovers: Pre-portion almonds into 1-ounce containers for the week.

name: Cucumber Rounds with Peanut Butter

ingredients.name: natural peanut butter (unsalted, no added sugar)

steps: Spread 1 tablespoon of natural peanut butter over cucumber rounds. One tablespoon is the portion — measure it.
Eat right away. Savory, not sweet, and surprisingly satisfying.
leftovers: Assemble fresh so the cucumber stays crisp.

name: Lemon-Pepper Avocado
steps: Halve an avocado and keep one half (wrap the rest with the pit in for later).
Season the cut side with lemon, pepper, and a tiny pinch of salt. Eat with a spoon.
leftovers: A half avocado is the right snack portion. The other half keeps until the next day with lemon and tight wrap.

name: Turkey & Cucumber Roll-Ups

ingredients.name: cooked turkey breast, sliced (not deli meat)

steps: Use leftover roasted turkey breast, not packaged deli slices.
Wrap cucumber sticks in the turkey, add lemon and pepper, and eat.
leftovers: Keep cooked turkey in the fridge for 3 days and roll these up in a minute.

name: Lemon Herb Shrimp
steps: Cook the shrimp in the oil with garlic and pepper, 1–2 minutes per side, until just opaque. No extra salt.
Toss with lemon and parsley. Eat warm or chilled, like a clean shrimp cocktail without sweet sauce.
leftovers: Make a batch and chill for 1–2 days. A high-protein snack with almost no saturated fat.

name: Cinnamon Walnuts
steps: Toast 1 ounce of walnuts in a dry skillet over medium-low heat, 4–6 minutes, tossing often, until fragrant. Don't walk away — they burn quickly.
Toss with cinnamon. Let cool a minute. Stick to 1 ounce.
leftovers: Toast a few 1-ounce portions and store in small containers.

name: Plain Protein Shake

ingredients.name: clean unsweetened protein powder (Previnex or similar)

steps: Shake or blend the protein powder with water and ice. Add a pinch of cinnamon if you want a little aroma.
This will taste like unsweetened protein, not a milkshake. That is by design.
leftovers: Mix fresh. Handy after a workout or when dinner will be late.

name: Bell Pepper Strips with Herbed Oil
steps: Cut the pepper into strips.
Stir the oil with oregano, lemon, and a tiny pinch of salt. Dip or drizzle lightly — 1 teaspoon of oil is enough.
leftovers: Cut peppers keep 2–3 days in the fridge. Mix the oil when you eat.

name: Measured Mixed Nuts
steps: Combine 1 ounce total of unsalted almonds, walnuts, and peanuts. Measure on a scale if you have one; otherwise use a small handful that fits in your cupped palm.
This mix skips macadamias, which are higher in saturated fat. Eat slowly.
leftovers: Pre-portion 1-ounce bags for the week so you never eat from a large jar.

name: Baked Kale Chips

ingredients.name: kale, stems removed, torn into pieces

steps: Heat the oven to 300°F. Dry the kale well, then toss with oil, garlic powder, and a tiny pinch of salt. Spread in a single layer.
Bake 12–15 minutes until crisp but not browned. They go from done to burned quickly.
Cool and eat. This recipe is two modest servings.
leftovers: Best the day you bake them. Store in a loosely covered bowl, not a sealed bag, or they soften.

name: Steamed Broccoli with Lemon-Herb Oil
steps: Steam the broccoli until tender-crisp, 5–6 minutes.
Toss with the oil, lemon, garlic powder, and pepper. Eat warm.
leftovers: You can steam a larger batch and dress a single serving when you want it.

name: Cucumber Boats with Turkey-Avocado

ingredients.name: cooked turkey breast, chopped (not deli meat)

steps: Halve the cucumber lengthwise and scoop out the seeds to make two boats.
Mash the avocado with lemon, herbs, and pepper. Stir in the chopped leftover turkey and fill the boats.
leftovers: Fill just before eating so the cucumber stays firm. The turkey mix keeps a day if you add the avocado fresh.

name: Garlic Roasted Mushrooms
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the mushrooms with oil, garlic, thyme, pepper, and a pinch of salt. Spread on a pan.
Roast 16–18 minutes until browned and the liquid has cooked off. This recipe is two servings — share or save half.
leftovers: Good warm or cold the next day. A savory snack when you want something warm without much fat.

name: Thick Cinnamon Protein Pudding

ingredients.name: clean unsweetened protein powder (Previnex or similar)
natural almond butter (no added sugar or oils)

steps: Stir the protein powder with just enough water to make a thick pudding. Mix in cinnamon and the teaspoon of almond butter.
This is mild and spiced, not sweet. Eat with a spoon.
leftovers: Mix fresh. A useful mid-afternoon snack when you need protein, not a pile of nuts.

name: Roasted Spiced Brussels Sprouts
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the sprouts with oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and a pinch of salt.
Roast 18–20 minutes until browned and crisp at the edges. Two servings — they disappear fast, so plate your share.
leftovers: Crispiest fresh from the oven; still good reheated in a hot skillet the next day.

name: Iced Tea & a Few Macadamias
steps: Brew unsweetened tea and pour it over ice, or use unsweetened bottled tea with no added sugar.
Portion 1/2 ounce of macadamias — about 5 or 6 nuts. That smaller portion is on purpose: macadamias are higher in saturated fat than almonds or walnuts.
leftovers: Keep a 1/2-ounce portion ready so you don't overpour from the jar.

name: Cinnamon Toasted Walnuts
steps: Toast 1 ounce of walnuts in a dry skillet over medium-low heat until fragrant, 4–6 minutes.
Toss with cinnamon and a pinch of nutmeg. Let cool slightly.
Treat-style, not sweet. You get warmth and spice, not dessert-level sweetness. Stick to 1 ounce.
leftovers: Toast portions ahead. This is a measured treat, not a bowl to graze from.
dessertNote: Treat-style, not sweet. Toasty and spiced only.

name: Avocado Cocoa Mousse

ingredients.name: clean unsweetened protein powder (Previnex or similar)

steps: Mash or blend the avocado with protein powder, cinnamon, vanilla, and just enough water to make a thick mousse.
Add unsweetened cocoa if you want a chocolate note — it is optional and unsweetened, so the result is cocoa-forward and mild, not a sweet pudding.
Treat-style, not sweet. Chill 10 minutes if you like it colder.
leftovers: Best within a few hours; avocado can dull in color. Press plastic wrap onto the surface if you refrigerate it.
dessertNote: Treat-style, not sweet. Cocoa-forward and mild. Skip the cocoa if you prefer.

name: Peanut Butter Protein Bites

ingredients.name: natural peanut butter (unsalted, no added sugar)
clean unsweetened protein powder (Previnex or similar)

steps: Stir the peanut butter, protein powder, cinnamon, and vanilla. Add water a few drops at a time until the mixture holds together.
Form 4 small bites and press a few chopped peanuts on top. One serving is 2 bites.
Treat-style, not sweet. Nutty and dense, like a savory-leaning protein bite.
leftovers: Keeps 3–4 days in the fridge. Nutrition is for 2 of the 4 bites.
dessertNote: Treat-style, not sweet. Nutty and dense. Serving is 2 bites.

name: Warm Spiced Almonds
steps: Toast 1 ounce of almonds in a dry skillet until fragrant, 5–6 minutes.
Toss with cinnamon and, if you like, a tiny pinch of cayenne or smoked paprika for a warm finish.
Treat-style, not sweet. Eat them warm, and stick to the ounce.
leftovers: Best warm. You can toast a few portions and rewarm briefly.
dessertNote: Treat-style, not sweet. Warm spice, no sugar.

name: No-Bake Cinnamon Nut Stacks

ingredients.name: natural almond butter (no added sugar or oils)
clean unsweetened protein powder (Previnex or similar)

steps: Stir the almond butter, protein powder, cinnamon, and vanilla into a thick paste. Fold in the chopped walnuts.
Press into two small stacks or one small patty. Eat with a fork.
Treat-style, not sweet. More nut shop than bakery.
leftovers: Can be chilled for an hour to firm up. Eat the same day.
dessertNote: Treat-style, not sweet. A small nut-and-spice bite.

name: Vanilla-Cinnamon Protein Pudding

ingredients.name: clean unsweetened protein powder (Previnex or similar)

steps: Stir the protein powder with just enough water to make a thick pudding. Mix in vanilla and cinnamon.
Top with a small sprinkle of walnuts.
Treat-style, not sweet. Mild, spiced, and high in protein — closer to a seasoned pudding than a dessert.
leftovers: Mix fresh. A better nightly treat if you want protein without another handful of nuts.
dessertNote: Treat-style, not sweet. Mild and spiced.

name: Espresso Walnut Bites

ingredients.name: clean unsweetened protein powder (Previnex or similar)

steps: Stir the chopped walnuts with protein powder, cinnamon, and just enough cooled coffee to hold the mix together.
Press into 3 small bites. Chill 10 minutes if you want them firmer.
Treat-style, not sweet. Coffee and walnut are the whole flavor.
leftovers: Keep a day in the fridge. Use leftover morning coffee.
dessertNote: Treat-style, not sweet. Coffee-and-walnut flavor only.

name: Frozen Cocoa-Peanut Butter Bites

ingredients.name: natural peanut butter (unsalted, no added sugar)
clean unsweetened protein powder (Previnex or similar)

steps: Stir the peanut butter with cinnamon, protein powder, and optional unsweetened cocoa. Form two small mounds on a parchment-lined plate.
Freeze about 30 minutes, until firm. Active time is only a few minutes.
Treat-style, not sweet. The freezer gives them a candy-like bite without any sweetener. Skip the cocoa if you don't keep it around.
leftovers: Keep frozen and eat straight from the freezer. Don't leave them out or they soften.
dessertNote: Treat-style, not sweet. Optional unsweetened cocoa only.

name: Mint Cocoa Almond Mash

ingredients.name: natural almond butter (no added sugar or oils)

steps: Stir the almond butter with optional cocoa, chopped fresh mint, and a drop of vanilla.
Eat with a spoon, slowly.
Treat-style, not sweet. Fresh mint is the lift; there is no mint candy flavor here.
leftovers: Mix fresh so the mint stays bright. One tablespoon of almond butter is the whole serving.
dessertNote: Treat-style, not sweet. Fresh mint, optional unsweetened cocoa.

name: Warm Walnut-Cinnamon Skillet Crumble

ingredients.name: clean unsweetened protein powder (Previnex or similar)

steps: Stir the protein powder with a little water and cinnamon to make a thick dollop. Spoon into a small bowl.
Warm the chopped walnuts in a dry skillet with the remaining cinnamon and a pinch of nutmeg, 2–3 minutes, until fragrant.
Scatter the warm walnuts over the pudding. Treat-style, not sweet — a warm crumble without a sugary filling.
leftovers: Toast the walnuts fresh. The pudding can be mixed while the pan heats.
dessertNote: Treat-style, not sweet. Warm spice over a mild protein pudding.
